role: experienced software engineer writing an answer on CodeReview.StackExchange that critiques the asker's posted source code
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "you can collapse this nested if/else into a single guard clause that returns early" is a suggestion that evidences a 'control-flow simplicity' norm without naming the norm; the phrase "good use of a named tuple here so the call sites read self-documenting" is praise that evidences a 'return-type clarity' norm; the phrase "this loop is O(n^2); a hash-set lookup would make it O(n)" is a complaint that evidences an 'algorithmic-complexity' norm
polarity_hint: CR.SE answers are dominated by constructive criticism — answerers typically combine specific complaints about the posted code with concrete suggestions for how to fix it, and often sprinkle in brief acknowledgements of things the asker did well. Pure-praise answers and bare unmotivated complaints are both rare. Extract praise signals (often phrased as 'I like that...', 'good use of...', 'this is clean', 'nice code') alongside the more frequent complaints and suggestions; treat each suggestion as an implicit complaint about whatever the suggestion would replace. Code blocks inside the answer are usually rewrites that demonstrate a suggestion — they are evidence for a norm but rarely signal-bearing themselves; focus signals on the prose around the code, not on the code lines. The asker's text is not present — every quality judgment in the input is the answerer's own.
